intro: Selke Pest Control provides residential pest control in Concord, North Carolina, including general pest control, mosquito control, flea and tick control, and rodent control. Concord is the seat of Cabarrus County and one of the fastest-growing cities in the Charlotte region, with more than 100,000 residents. That growth is exactly why pest pressure is so high here: new subdivisions are built on former farmland and wooded tracts, disturbed soil invites fire ants, and the creek corridors that run through the city give mosquitoes and ticks a direct path into backyards. As a family-owned company based in nearby Mooresville, Selke Pest Control treats Concord homes with the same thorough, more-than-56-minute service we deliver across Lake Norman, backed by the Selke Guarantee.
geographyPest: Concord sits in the rolling Piedmont northeast of Charlotte, where the Rocky River, Coddle Creek, and Irish Buffalo Creek and their tributaries drain through residential areas. Those creek buffers stay shaded and humid, which lets mosquitoes rest during the day and ticks survive along wooded lot lines. Heavy red clay soils hold water after summer storms, so low spots, French drains, and retention ponds turn into mosquito breeding sites within days. Older homes near Historic Downtown Concord have mature trees and crawl spaces that favor carpenter ants, spiders, and moisture pests, while newer communities around Christenbury, Moss Creek, and the Concord Mills area deal with fire ants and rodents displaced by construction.

topPests.name: Mosquitoes
topPests.description: Concord mosquito season usually runs from April through October. Asian tiger mosquitoes bite during the day and breed in small containers like planters, toys, and clogged gutters, while Culex mosquitoes breed in retention ponds and drainage areas near the Rocky River and its creeks. Monthly barrier treatments during the warm season target the shaded vegetation where adult mosquitoes rest.

topPests.name: Fire Ants
topPests.description: Fire ants are one of the most common complaints in Concord because so many lawns are newly graded. Colonies spread quickly through open, sunny yards and common areas, and their stings are a real risk for children and pets. Property-wide treatment works better than treating individual mounds.

topPests.name: Ticks
topPests.description: Lone star ticks, American dog ticks, and black-legged ticks are active in Cabarrus County from March through November. Wooded edges, creek buffers, and tall grass around Concord neighborhoods and parks such as Frank Liske Park are the highest-risk areas for families and pets.

topPests.name: Rodents
topPests.description: As development replaces farmland and woods around Concord, house mice and rats move into garages, attics, and crawl spaces, especially from October through February. Sealing entry points and setting a monitored perimeter keeps them out.

neighborhoods.name: Moss Creek
neighborhoods.pestNote: Moss Creek has ponds, walking trails, and wooded common areas that support mosquitoes and ticks through the warm season. Backyards that border the trails benefit most from monthly mosquito barrier treatments.

neighborhoods.pestNote: Afton Village is a walkable, traditional neighborhood with closely spaced homes, irrigated landscaping, and pocket parks. Ants and spiders move easily between homes, and irrigated beds hold moisture that attracts mosquitoes and occasional invaders.

neighborhoods.name: Christenbury
neighborhoods.pestNote: Christenbury, near the Mecklenburg County line, includes newer construction with freshly graded lawns and wooded buffers. Fire ants and ticks are the most common problems, along with ants entering along slab foundations.

neighborhoods.name: Historic Downtown Concord
neighborhoods.pestNote: Homes near Union Street and the historic district are older, with crawl spaces, mature hardwoods, and original wood trim. That combination favors carpenter ants, spiders, cockroaches, and mice looking for warmth in the fall.

neighborhoods.name: Concord Mills & Speedway Area
neighborhoods.pestNote: Neighborhoods near Concord Mills and Charlotte Motor Speedway sit close to commercial corridors and active construction, which pushes rodents and cockroaches toward nearby homes. Perimeter treatments and exclusion work help prevent spillover.

seasonalTips: In Concord, start mosquito treatments in April before populations build, and keep them going monthly through October. Spring is ant swarm and fire ant season, so treat lawns early. Summer storms leave standing water in clay soil, so empty containers and clean gutters within a few days of heavy rain. In fall, have the perimeter inspected and gaps sealed before mice and rats move indoors. Quarterly general pest control keeps ants, spiders, and cockroaches out year-round.

intro: Selke Pest Control provides residential pest control in Mount Ulla, North Carolina, including general pest control, tick control, mosquito control, and rodent control. Mount Ulla is a rural, unincorporated community in western Rowan County, just east of Mooresville and the Iredell County line. Homes here often sit on acreage next to pastures, ponds, barns, and hardwood tree lines, which means pest problems look very different than they do in a suburban subdivision. Because Selke Pest Control is based in nearby Mooresville, we can reach Mount Ulla quickly and we understand how to protect country properties without cutting corners.
geographyPest: Mount Ulla sits in the rolling farmland of the western Rowan County Piedmont, along the NC Highway 801 corridor between Mooresville and Salisbury. Open pasture, hay fields, livestock water, farm ponds, and wooded creek bottoms create year-round habitat for ticks, rodents, and stinging insects. Ticks wait in tall grass along field edges and tree lines, mice and rats shelter in barns and feed storage before moving into homes in the fall, and ponds and water troughs produce mosquitoes all summer. Wasps, hornets, and yellow jackets build nests under eaves, porches, and outbuildings.

topPests.name: Stinging Insects
topPests.description: Paper wasps, hornets, and yellow jackets nest under eaves, porch ceilings, barn rafters, and in the ground. We treat and remove active nests around the home and help prevent new ones.

neighborhoods.name: Farm & Equestrian Properties
neighborhoods.pestNote: Barns, feed rooms, and livestock water create ideal conditions for rodents, flies, and mosquitoes. A perimeter plan around the home and nearby outbuildings keeps pests from moving inside.
